Trail Notes

Fixing a squeaky bike chain

A squeaky chain is almost always a dry chain. Before you reach for oil, shift into a middle gear, hold a rag around the lower run of the chain and turn the pedals backwards for a minute to wipe off the old grit.

Next, put one small drop of chain lube on each roller while you turn the cranks slowly. More is not better: extra oil only collects dirt, which turns into a grinding paste within a week of riding on gravel.

Let the lube soak in for five minutes, then wipe the outside of the chain again with a clean rag. The lube belongs inside the rollers, not on the side plates where it picks up dust and drips onto the wheel.

If the squeak comes back after a ride or two, check for a stiff link by turning the cranks backwards and watching the chain run through the rear derailleur. A link that jumps is the culprit, and a little flex by hand frees it.
